regulatory.claim: Article 12(1) requires high-risk AI systems to technically allow automatic recording of events (logs) over the system lifetime.
Article 12(2) says logging must support traceability, identifying risk or substantial modification, post-market monitoring, and deployer monitoring.
For Annex III 1(a) biometric systems, Article 12(3) expressly requires start/end time of each use, reference database, matched input data, and identification of human verifiers.
Article 50 applies from 2 August 2026 and requires people to be informed when interacting with covered AI systems unless obvious.

Article 50(2) requires providers of systems generating synthetic audio, image, video, or text to mark outputs in a machine-readable, detectable form, subject to stated exceptions and technical feasibility.
Article 50(4) requires deployers to disclose deepfakes and certain AI-generated public-interest text, subject to stated exceptions.

Official Commission timeline: prohibited-practice and AI-literacy obligations applied 2 February 2025; governance and GPAI obligations applied 2 August 2025; the Act generally applied 2 August 2026; Annex III high-risk rules apply 2 December 2027; Annex I embedded-product high-risk rules apply 2 August 2028.
Article 99 penalty ceiling for prohibited practices is EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher for undertakings.
Article 99 penalty ceiling for listed operator duties and Article 50 transparency breaches is EUR 15 million or 3% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher for undertakings.

Article 99 penalty ceiling for incorrect, incomplete, or misleading information to notified bodies or national authorities is EUR 7.5 million or 1% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher for undertakings; SME ceilings use the lower amount or percentage.

pricing_recommendation.rationale: ANALYST ESTIMATE, not a published transaction price: recommend USD 500–2,500 per independently checkable attested inference-run artifact. This sits above commodity timestamp/provenance primitives (free OpenTimestamps, USD 0.0008 Hedera messages, and sub-cent C2PA signatures: https://opentimestamps.org/ ; https://docs.hedera.com/networks/fees ; https://console.originalpictures.com/) because the offer includes computation identity, timing, substrate, and reconstruction evidence, but below broader human compliance audits (USD 2,249 quick audit and USD 7,499 standard audit: https://eucomplyhub.com/pricing) and SOC 2-style reports (starting USD 3,000–7,000: https://auditsuisse.com/soc-2-pricing). Use the low end for a standardized self-serve receipt and the high end for a bespoke, independently reviewed evidence bundle; enterprise volume contracts should be quoted separately. No public sale price for the Commons offer was verified.
